_note: GROUND TRUTH for the cloud cron fleet. Never regenerate this from the live scheduler - that would make the check agree with the corruption. Reconstructed from migration-state.json (the 2026-09-25 snapshot of the source mavis cron list = the ORIGINAL local Windows crons of record) plus the deliberate post-migration changes documented in cloud-prompts/cron-prompts/README.md and each prompt's ## SCHEDULE block. #91 is the drift guard itself: a DAILY cron, deliberately, so a GUI save cannot narrow it.
_why: Saving a scheduled task in the agent.minimax.io web GUI silently collapses the day-of-week field of a weekday routine: 1-5 (Mon-Fri) becomes 1 (Mondays only). Measured 2026-10-31 on cron #26: a GUI save that changed ONLY the model effort rewrote 30 8 * * 1-5 to 30 8 * * 1. On 2026-10-31 the same corruption hit 14 routines in a 05:40-09:08 ET sweep. The corruption is SILENT because next_run does not change (both forms next-fire on Monday).
_invariant: Every weekday routine is 1-5. Only genuinely weekly routines carry a single day (0=Sun, 3=Wed, 6=Sat). #90 is daily.

session_mode_invariant.why: Every routine must create a FRESH conversation per fire. A routine bound to a fixed conversation (session.mode=sessionId) piles every run into one thread, which breaks the fresh-session/ephemeral-artifact contract the artifact routines depend on and makes the sidebar unreadable. Verified 2026-11-02: all 25 routines were session.mode=new with an empty session_id. A web-GUI save can flip this the same way it collapses the day-of-week field, so cron #91 checks it every day and REPORTS it - it never auto-repairs a session binding, because a fixed conversation can be a deliberate choice.
